What is Music?
Music is a creative and expressive subject that enables pupils to listen, perform, compose and respond to music. It helps pupils understand how sounds are created, organised and communicated while experiencing music from a wide range of styles, traditions, cultures and periods.
The Kapow Primary Music scheme provides a spiral curriculum from EYFS to Year 6, with learning organised around the interrelated dimensions of music. The current curriculum is structured through five key strands:
Listening and evaluating.
Creating sound.
Notation.
Improvising and composing.
Performing.
Why is Music important?
Music gives every child opportunities to be creative, expressive and actively involved in making music. Pupils learn to use their voices and instruments, listen carefully, create and develop musical ideas and perform both individually and with others.
Through our spiral curriculum, pupils revisit and build upon prior learning so that they know more, remember more and can do more as musicians. They develop increasingly accurate musical vocabulary and learn to perform with greater accuracy, fluency, control and expression, improvise and compose for different purposes and understand and use musical notation.
Listening and evaluating are integral to our curriculum. Pupils experience a broad range of high-quality music from different styles, periods, traditions, composers and musicians. They learn to listen with increasing attention to detail, respond thoughtfully and use their growing knowledge of the inter-related dimensions of music to discuss what they hear.
We believe Music should be accessible to all pupils. Children work towards the same ambitious musical learning, with appropriate support, modelling, scaffolding and challenge enabling every pupil to participate and succeed.
Music also develops wider skills including confidence, creativity, concentration, communication, teamwork and perseverance. Pupils have opportunities to perform and celebrate their musical achievements with others.
SMSC
Music provides rich opportunities for pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development. Pupils express ideas and emotions, listen and respond to the work of others and learn to value different musical traditions and cultures. Collaborative composing and performing encourage cooperation, respect and a sense of belonging, while a diverse musical repertoire helps pupils appreciate the richness of the wider world.

Our vision
At Uplands, our vision is to create a vibrant and inclusive school community where every child is inspired to achieve their full potential. We aim to ignite a lifelong love of learning and empower our pupils to embrace challenges with confidence, creativity, and determination. By fostering ambition and celebrating achievements, we prepare our children to thrive in a rapidly changing world.
We are dedicated to ensuring that every classroom is led by an exceptional teacher who delivers an engaging and ambitious curriculum. Supported by effective systems for behaviour and care, we provide the foundation for all pupils to excel academically, socially, and emotionally.
Our School Vision and Values, ensuring that all children at Uplands flourish, underpin everything we do at school.

Respectful
Kind
Resilient
Brave
Motivated
Behaviour Expectations
At our school, we believe that positive behaviour is essential for creating a safe, respectful and inclusive environment where every pupil can learn, grow and achieve their best.
We expect all members of our school community to treat one another with kindness, courtesy and respect. Pupils are encouraged to take responsibility for their choices, listen to others, follow school routines and demonstrate a positive attitude towards learning.

We recognise and celebrate positive behaviour, while responding fairly and consistently when expectations are not met and more detail on how we manage this is in our behaviour policy below.
We work in partnership with parents and carers to support pupils in developing the skills, confidence and self-discipline they need to succeed both in school and beyond.
Together, we can ensure that our school is a place where everyone feels respected, supported and able to thrive.

Computing
Our Computing curriculum has been designed to encourage pupils to become curious, creative and confident thinkers. We want children to develop a broad understanding of how technology works and how it influences the world around us.
Through our Computing lessons, pupils are encouraged to ask questions, explore ideas, solve problems and develop practical skills. They learn how to use technology purposefully, analyse information and create and present their own digital content.
We use the Kapow Computing curriculum, which helps pupils understand how computing and technology shape our lives, both now and in the past. Through this, we aim to develop resourceful and responsible digital citizens who have the knowledge and skills to use technology safely, confidently and creatively.

What is Geography?
Geography is the study of places, people and environments and the relationships between them. It helps pupils understand the world around them, from their local area to places and environments across the globe.
The Kapow Primary Geography scheme provides a progressive journey from EYFS to Key Stage 2, developing essential geographical concepts while encouraging curiosity and exploration. Learning is organised through four key strands:
Locational knowledge.
Place knowledge.
Human and physical geography.
Geographical skills and fieldwork.
Why is Geography important?
Geography encourages pupils to be curious about the world and to understand their place within it. Pupils learn about different people, places, cultures and environments while developing an appreciation of both similarities and differences.
Through geographical enquiry and fieldwork, pupils learn to use maps, atlases, globes and digital mapping, collect and present data, observe human and physical features and communicate their findings. As they move through school, pupils build on prior learning and develop increasingly secure geographical knowledge and skills.
The curriculum also enables pupils to explore important issues such as sustainability, climate, natural resources, settlements and the ways in which people and environments affect one another. This supports pupils in becoming informed, responsible and thoughtful citizens.
SMSC
Geography provides regular opportunities for pupils to explore different perspectives, cultures and ways of life. Pupils consider environmental and ethical issues, work collaboratively during enquiry and fieldwork and develop respect for communities locally and around the world. It encourages pupils to reflect on their responsibilities towards other people and the planet.

What is PSHE & RSE?
Relationships and Sex Education. Schools may use different names for these subjects: RSE may be referred to as RSHE when health education is included; similarly, PSHE may be referred to as PSHCE when citizenship is included.
The Kapow Primary RSE & PSHE scheme covers the full breadth of learning pupils need to stay healthy, safe and prepared for life. This includes:
Personal.
Economic.
Relationships.
Citizenship.
Sex education (optional).
Why is RSE & PSHE important?
RSE & PSHE education helps pupils maintain their mental and physical health and understand the various factors that influence their wellbeing. They learn how to build strong and supportive relationships, how to keep themselves safe in various situations and how to make thoughtful decisions about money, health and the online world.
Pupils may receive mixed messages about these topics from friends, siblings, social media and the wider world. High-quality RSE & PSHE ensures every child receives clear, accurate and age-appropriate teaching so they can make safe and informed choices as they grow.
SMSC
RSE & PSHE gives pupils regular opportunities to explore different perspectives, reflect on ethical and emotional issues and think about what is right and fair. Pupils collaborate with others, build positive relationships and learn to value and respect people from different backgrounds, families and cultures.
It is important to note that SMSC development does not occur solely through RSE & PSHE but is woven throughout the entire curriculum and the wider life of the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher Welcome Message - Uplands Primary School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
Headteacher Welcome Message
Uplands opened in 1962 and was built on the site of ‘Uplands House’. We are a one-form-entry primary school in Sandhurst, Berkshire, with a nursery onsite. Uplands Primary School and Nursery is the lead school of the Forest Learning Alliance and we are proud members of the Keys Academy Trust. We are dedicated to having and ensuring high standards for pupils and staff, as well as a culture of support and challenge.
We have recently expanded our Nursery provision to be able to welcome children from 2 years old and so Uplands really can provide an all-through option for parents and families across our community.
Our key behaviours (We are Respectful, Kind, Resilient, Brave and Motivated), which were created by staff, pupils, parents/carers and governors, underpin all that we do, and all stakeholders live and work by these values. Our vision is simply ‘for all to be inspired to achieve’, as we felt this could apply to all the pupils, staff, governors and members of our Forest Learning Alliance. Our children are at the heart of all our decisions, and we are committed to providing the best possible education for them.At Uplands, we enjoy planning exciting, creative lessons and ensure that children have a chance to succeed in all areas of life. This means that all subjects are given importance and are taught in full. In addition to the core subjects of English, Maths and Science, children at Uplands have the opportunity to explore music, arts, sports and more within the school day, and our wide range of extra-curricular activities supports the development of children’s interests out of school.
Our end of Key Stage assessment results (EYFS, KS1, Phonics Screening Check and KS2) have been consistently high for many years, which is made easier by exemplary behaviour, leading to excellent outcomes. Behaviour is taken very seriously, as well as safeguarding, to ensure children feel safe and happy. The staff and governors are highly skilled and committed to ensuring we provide the very best education we can.
We are a caring community, with staff and our families referring to the school as a ‘family’, and our children are proud and happy to be at Uplands. “Inspired to Achieve” is our motto, and staff are committed to supporting all children, regardless of ability or SEND, to achieve their best and reach age-related expectations and beyond.

Uplands Nursery
Join Us
Our Admissions Process
Uplands Nursery
Welcome to our Nursery
We are entering an exciting new phase of our Nursery’s journey after being awarded one of the first DfE Grants to expand our provision to wider serve the needs of our community.
After undergoing extensive renovation works (which you can see in the presentation below), we now have provision to welcome 2-year-olds from January 2026.
You will see from the pictures that we now have two rooms that are fully fit for purpose and split into the Acorns room for 2-3 year olds and the Oaks room for our 3-4 year olds, although there will be opportunities to interact with the different age groups where appropriate.
As part of the renovations, the Nursery now has fully renovated rooms and furniture, a wonderful new play area, new toilets and outdoor learning areas, all of which will serve to build on our already strong foundations at Uplands.
Uplands Nursery occupies a self-contained building within the Uplands Primary School site and accepts children, usually from the term after their second birthday, or if there are places available, as soon as they reach the age of two.
At Uplands, we understand that deciding on nursery provision for your child is an important process for parents and carers, and that many factors need to be taken into consideration. We aim to provide the best possible start to each and every child’s education and we are very proud of the work we do. Children attending Uplands Nursery have an excellent opportunity to commence their education in close association with our highly successful school from the age of 2. Whilst Uplands Nursery is a separate entity in regards to admissions, it is very much a part of the Uplands family. This brings the added advantages of access to many of the schools resources, such as the school hall, the purpose-built cookery room, field, playground and trim trail, as well as having the opportunity to mix with the community of Uplands Primary School and Nursery.
At Uplands Nursery, your child will be able to benefit from working with a fully-qualified teacher alongside other highly qualified Early Year practitioners. Some of the exciting opportunities that children will be able to experience include PE sessions with our Sports Coach, Outdoor Adventures sessions in our little patch of woodland, weekly engaging phonics activities, exciting trips out and visitors booked to come to us, cooking in our cookery room and our annual Sports Day.
We enable pupils to have the best start in education by: promoting independence and confidence; monitoring and developing key personal and academic skills; celebrating and modelling core values; and nurturing a love of learning. The skills and values that we promote prepare every child for transition into primary school.
We are also embracing EYFS Development Matters.
We accept government funding and invite potential parents to look here to check eligibility for their child.
Homepage | Best Start in Life
To claim the extended hours of government funding, all applications must be made in the term before you wish to use the funding. For example, if you have applied to Uplands Nursery for your child to attend in the Spring term (January) you must have accessed the Government website and made your application for funding in the Autumn term (before 31st December).
Session times are as follows:
Morning: 08:45 – 11:45Lunchtime: 11:45 – 12:30Afternoon: 12:30 – 15:30
If you would like more information about Uplands Nursery, please contact us.
Please note: Obtaining a place at Uplands Nursery will not give children priority for a place at Uplands Primary School. All school applications are made through Bracknell Forest School Admissions.
